Mia Chen: Putting together a dashboard for model SKU economics — need token-level cost, cache savings attribution, and amortized infra per model. Thinking of a per-route + per-model rollup. Anyone see pitfalls?
Jordan Patel: Love it. Two quick Qs: how are we defining "token cost"? raw compute token vs billable token? Also caching: do we credit savings to the route that hit the cache or to the model that served the cached reply?
Mia Chen: Good call — we want billable tokens (what we charge customers) as the baseline, then overlay compute cost derived from model SKU/instance-hours + token throughput.
Samir Rao: For cache attribution I favor proportional split: allocate cache savings along the satisfied route's token footprint in the time window. Simpler than trying to backtrace to origin model for multi-hop responses.
Rachel Li: Edge case: multi-model responses (tool-calling). If route A calls model B then returns to A, who gets the cache credit? My vote: primary route gets the credit but tag the dependent models for audit.
Jordan Patel: Implementation note: we should expose two numbers: "gross token cost" and "net after cache". Also add a "cache-credit" column per-route and a column for "cache-hit-rate by prefix".
Mia Chen: Agreed. Also want a column for "amortized infra per-token" — compute as (reserved GPU cost * share_factor) / tokens_served. Share_factor could be model-weighted or route-weighted.
Samir Rao: Prefer model-weighted for Dedicated pools, route-weighted for Hosted where many tenants share. We need flagging logic based on deployment mode.
cost-bot: FYI historical data shows caching reduces token compute by ~27% for conversational workloads (sample window 30d).
Rachel Li: UX: make per-model SKU rows collapsible into per-route views. When a route spans multiple SKUs show a small sparkline for price variance over time.
Jordan Patel: Telemetry hook: are we sampling per-token traces? full per-token telemetry is heavy. Propose 1% sampling with deterministic hashing by request-id to ensure consistent grouping.
Mia Chen: Good. Also need to handle quotas — when we show amortized infra, we should exclude tokens blocked by quota throttles (they still count towards cost but not served?). Open question.
Samir Rao: Throttled requests still consumed compute? Usually not. We should exclude requests rejected before hitting runtime; include partials that executed.
Rachel Li: Action items: (1) Mia to mock a dashboard wireframe, (2) Jordan to spec telemetry and sampling, (3) Samir to propose attribution algorithm and SQL for rollups, (4) Rachel to write UX collapse rules + edgecases doc. Ping in two days.
Mia Chen: I'll post a Figma link once ready. thanks everyone :pray: 
devops-bot: Deploy scheduled: cost-metrics/collector v2 -> staging at 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC :rocket:
Mia Chen: noted, will sync with Jordan for telemetry changes before that deploy.
